══ WORKED TEXTBOOK EXAMPLES ══

1. How can you show that a colourless liquid contains water? Is this a test for pure water?
   Solution: Add a few drops to white anhydrous copper(II) sulphate; it turns blue if water is present (CuSO₄ + 5H₂O → CuSO₄·5H₂O). It does not show purity; to test purity check that the liquid melts at exactly 0 °C and boils at exactly 100 °C.
chapters.solvedExercises:
NBF Chapter 12 Exercises (175–176):

— Exercise MCQs —
i. Which of the following is not a water-borne disease? → D (anaemia) | Anaemia is caused by lack of iron/haemoglobin, not by water microbes.
ii. Which human activity results in contamination of water bodies? → D (all of these) | All pollute water.
iii. pH of distilled water is: → A (7) | Pure water is neutral.
iv. Anhydrous copper(II) sulphate is a ____ solid. → B (white) | Hydrated is blue; anhydrous is white.

— Q2. Give short answers —
(i) List the impurities present in rain water.
   Answer: Dissolved gases: CO₂ (carbonic acid), SO₂ and NOₓ (sulphuric and nitric acids – acid rain), oxygen and nitrogen; dust, soot and smoke particles; pollen and microbes picked up from the air.
(ii) List toxic substances present in household wastes.
   Answer: Detergents (phosphates), bleach and toilet cleaners, paints and solvents, pesticides and insecticides, batteries (mercury, cadmium, lead), expired medicines, plastics, motor oil.
(iii) In what ways do industrial wastes pollute water?
   Answer: Factories discharge heavy metals (Pb, Hg, Cr, As), acids and alkalis, dyes from textile mills, oil and grease, and hot water into rivers. These poison aquatic life, make water unfit to drink, reduce dissolved oxygen (thermal pollution) and enter the food chain.
(iv) What is water pollution?
   Answer: The contamination of water bodies (rivers, lakes, groundwater, sea) by harmful substances – sewage, chemicals, plastics, microbes – that make the water unsafe for humans and harmful to aquatic life.
(v) List some water-borne diseases.
   Answer: Cholera, typhoid, dysentery, hepatitis (jaundice), diarrhoea, polio.
(vi) What are pathogenic microorganisms?
   Answer: Microorganisms that cause disease: certain bacteria (e.g. Salmonella typhi, Vibrio cholerae), viruses (hepatitis, polio), protozoa (amoeba) and parasites found in contaminated water.

— Q3–Q11. Descriptive questions —
3. How does tap water differ from distilled water?
   Answer: See the table in topic 12.2: distilled water is made by distillation, contains no dissolved salts, has pH 7, hardly conducts electricity and is used for preparing solutions; tap water is treated natural water containing dissolved minerals and chlorine, conducts electricity, leaves a residue on evaporation and is used for drinking and washing.
4. Why are municipal water supplies treated with aluminium sulphate?
   Answer: Aluminium sulphate (alum) is a coagulant. It forms sticky aluminium hydroxide flakes that trap tiny suspended clay and dirt particles, making them clump into larger flocs that settle quickly during sedimentation and are easily filtered. This makes the water clear.
5. What are some health effects of biological contamination of water?
   Answer: Pathogens in contaminated water cause cholera (severe diarrhoea, dehydration), typhoid (high fever), dysentery (bloody diarrhoea), hepatitis A/E (jaundice, liver damage), polio and diarrhoea – which kills many young children. Outbreaks spread quickly in floods and crowded areas.
6. Identify the negative effects of water pollutants on life.
   Answer: Sewage → water-borne diseases; heavy metals (Pb, Hg, As) → poisoning, kidney and brain damage, cancer; nitrates and phosphates → eutrophication and fish deaths, nitrate poisoning in infants; plastics → animals choke, microplastics in food; oil spills → birds and fish killed; pesticides → accumulate in food chains; hot water → less dissolved oxygen.
7. Water scarcity is an important issue in Pakistan. Give your comments.
   Answer: Pakistan is water-stressed because of rapid population growth, climate change (irregular rain, melting glaciers, droughts and floods), over-pumping of groundwater, wasteful flood irrigation, too little storage and pollution of rivers. Solutions: efficient irrigation (drip, sprinkler, lined canals), new dams and rainwater harvesting, regulation of tube-wells, treatment and reuse of wastewater, and public awareness to stop wastage.
8. What are fertilizers?
   Answer: Substances added to soil to provide essential elements (mainly N, P and K) for plant growth and higher crop yields, e.g. urea, ammonium nitrate, ammonium sulphate, DAP, potassium nitrate and NPK mixtures.
9. Public health depends on water quality. Give arguments.
   Answer: Most diseases in developing countries are water-related; contaminated water spreads cholera, typhoid, hepatitis and diarrhoea; toxic metals and arsenic cause long-term illness and cancer; clean water reduces child deaths, medical costs and lost school/work days; safe water is needed for cooking and hygiene. Hence clean water is the foundation of public health.
10. How does chemistry help maintain a clean swimming pool?
   Answer: Chlorine (or sodium/calcium hypochlorite) is added: it forms hypochlorous acid HOCl, which kills bacteria and algae. The pH is kept at about 7.2–7.8 using acids or bases so chlorine works well and does not irritate eyes. Alum (flocculant) clumps fine dirt for filtration. Regular testing kits measure chlorine and pH.
11. It is advisable to wash hands well with soap after using bathrooms. Evaluate.
   Answer: Faeces carry pathogens (E. coli, Salmonella, hepatitis A virus). Hands pick them up and transfer them to food, water and the mouth. Soap molecules lift away grease and dirt containing germs and break the outer membranes of many microbes, so they are rinsed off. Studies show handwashing greatly reduces diarrhoea and typhoid – so it is a simple, cheap and very effective habit.
chapters.importantQuestions:
══ SHORT RESPONSE QUESTIONS (PAST PAPERS, MODEL PAPERS & SLO PRACTICE) ══

1. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] How are “dissolved oxygen” and “essential minerals” beneficial for aquatic life?
   Answer: Dissolved oxygen is needed by fish and other aquatic organisms for respiration (and by bacteria to break down waste). Essential minerals (compounds of Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn, Cu) supply elements for shells, bones, enzymes and growth of aquatic plants and animals.

2. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] Write benefits of dissolved oxygen and essential minerals found in water.
   Answer: Dissolved oxygen: supports respiration of aquatic life and decomposition of wastes. Minerals: Ca and Mg for bones and teeth, Fe for blood, Zn/Cu/Mn activate enzymes.

3. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] Why are sedimentation and chlorination used in water treatment?
   Answer: Sedimentation lets suspended solids settle (helped by alum) so the water becomes clear. Chlorination kills harmful bacteria and viruses so the water is safe to drink and stays safe in pipes.

4. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] Name the three main types of chemical fertilizers commonly used in agriculture.
   Answer: Nitrogen fertilizers (urea, ammonium nitrate), phosphorus fertilizers (DAP, superphosphate) and potassium fertilizers (potassium nitrate/sulphate) – together as NPK.

5. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] Name three nitrogen-containing fertilizers used in agriculture.
   Answer: Urea CO(NH₂)₂, ammonium nitrate NH₄NO₃, ammonium sulphate (NH₄)₂SO₄ (also DAP, CAN, KNO₃).

6. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026 (Old-22)] Briefly describe any two common water-borne diseases.
   Answer: Cholera: caused by Vibrio cholerae; severe watery diarrhoea and vomiting, dehydration. Typhoid: caused by Salmonella typhi; prolonged high fever, weakness, abdominal pain. Prevent by drinking boiled/chlorinated water and washing hands.

7. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026 (Old-22)] Enlist any three harmful substances that may be found in natural water sources.
   Answer: Toxic metal compounds (lead, mercury, arsenic); sewage with harmful microbes; nitrates and phosphates from fertilizers (also plastics, pesticides).

8. [Verified Official - FBISE 2nd Annual 2025] What are the sources of nitrates and phosphates found in water? Why are they considered harmful?
   Answer: Sources: fertilizer run-off from fields, detergents (phosphates), sewage and animal waste. Harmful: they cause eutrophication – algae grow rapidly, then die and decay, using up dissolved oxygen so fish die; high nitrate in drinking water harms infants.

9. [Verified Official - FBISE 2nd Annual 2025] Complete the table: disease, cause and symptoms for dysentery, typhoid and hepatitis.
   Answer: 

10. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] Suggest any three measures to control the water scarcity problem in Pakistan.
   Answer: Build dams/reservoirs and harvest rainwater; use drip and sprinkler irrigation and line canals; regulate groundwater extraction and treat/reuse wastewater (plus public awareness).

11. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] Briefly state any three causes of water scarcity in Pakistan.
   Answer: Rapid population growth; climate change (irregular rainfall, droughts); over-extraction of groundwater and wasteful flood irrigation.

12. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] What is meant by NPK fertilizers? Why are they used?
   Answer: Fertilizers that supply nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K). Used because these primary nutrients are needed in large amounts: N for leaves/stems and chlorophyll, P for roots, flowers and seeds, K for disease resistance and fruit quality – increasing crop yield.

13. [Verified Official - FBISE Model Paper (AF)] How do household wastes, agricultural wastes and metals (as water pollutants) affect living organisms?
   Answer: Household waste/sewage: microbes cause water-borne diseases and decay uses up oxygen. Agricultural waste: fertilizers cause eutrophication and pesticides poison aquatic life and enter food chains. Metals (Pb, Hg, As): toxic, damage kidneys and nerves, cause cancer and accumulate in fish.

14. [Verified Official - FBISE Model Paper (AF)] What are the primary nutrients provided by urea, ammonium salts and nitrates when used as fertilizers?
   Answer: All mainly provide nitrogen; potassium nitrate also provides potassium and ammonium phosphate also provides phosphorus.

15. [Verified Official - FBISE Model Paper (50%)] Differentiate between distilled water and tap water. How does the use of carbon improve the quality of drinking water beyond just removing visible impurities?
   Answer: Distilled: no dissolved salts, pH 7, non-conducting, for lab solutions. Tap: treated water with minerals and chlorine. Activated carbon adsorbs dissolved organic compounds and some chemicals (excess chlorine, pesticides), removing bad tastes, odours and colours that filtration cannot remove.

16. How can you test the purity of a water sample using melting and boiling points?
   Answer: Pure water melts sharply at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C (1 atm). Dissolved impurities lower the melting point and raise the boiling point, and the change happens over a range.

17. What is eutrophication?
   Answer: Excess nitrates/phosphates cause rapid algal growth; when algae die, decomposing bacteria use up dissolved oxygen, killing fish.


══ EXTENDED / LONG RESPONSE QUESTIONS ══

1. Explain the treatment of the domestic water supply.
   Answer: 1. Screening removes large floating objects.
2. Sedimentation with coagulation: alum (aluminium sulphate) makes fine particles clump; water stands in tanks so they settle.
3. Filtration through sand and gravel beds removes remaining particles.
4. Activated carbon removes tastes, odours and colours.
5. Chlorination kills harmful microbes (Cl₂ + H₂O → HCl + HOCl).
6. pH adjustment (and sometimes fluoridation), then storage and supply through pipes.

2. Describe the useful and harmful substances found in water from natural sources.
   Answer: Useful: dissolved oxygen (aquatic respiration), mineral compounds of Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn, Cu (bones, blood, enzymes). Harmful: toxic metal compounds (Pb, Hg, As), plastics (choke animals, microplastics), sewage with pathogens (cholera, typhoid), nitrates and phosphates (eutrophication, deoxygenation, infant health risk).

3. Explain the use of NPK fertilizers and how their careless use can pollute water.
   Answer: NPK supplies N (leafy growth, proteins, chlorophyll), P (roots, flowers, seeds, energy transfer) and K (disease resistance, fruit quality, water balance). Urea, ammonium salts and nitrates are N sources. Because they are soluble, excess fertilizer washes into rivers and lakes with rain (run-off), causing eutrophication; nitrates can seep into groundwater. Nutrient management – right amount, right time – avoids this.

4. Describe three main classes of biomolecules found in food… [see Ch 15] / Describe various water-borne diseases and the steps to avoid them.
   Answer: Diseases: cholera, typhoid, dysentery, hepatitis A/E, diarrhoea, polio – caused by pathogenic microbes in water contaminated with sewage. Prevention: boil/chlorinate/filter drinking water, wash hands with soap, proper sanitation and sewage treatment, separate sewage and water pipes, cover and clean tanks, wash food, vaccination.

chapters.title: Organic Chemistry
chapters.introduction:
Organic chemistry is the chemistry of carbon compounds – fuels, plastics, medicines, food and the molecules of life. This unit explains why carbon forms so many compounds (catenation), how organic molecules are straight-chain, branched or cyclic, how to write structural, condensed and molecular formulae, homologous series and their general formulae, structural isomers (C₄H₁₀, C₄H₈), saturated and unsaturated compounds, and the main functional groups: alcohols, phenols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, amines and amides.

Exam focus (9 summative SLOs): identify functional groups (CH₃COOH, CH₃CHO, CH₃CH₂OH appear repeatedly), general formulae of alkanes/alkenes/alkynes/alcohols/carboxylic acids, characteristics of a homologous series, isomers of C₄H₁₀ and C₄H₈, saturated vs unsaturated, classify alcohol/ether/phenol. The 50% model paper has 9 MCQs from this chapter.

Exam focus (9 summative SLOs): identify functional groups (CH₃COOH, CH₃CHO, CH₃CH₂OH appear repeatedly), general formulae of alkanes/alkenes/alkynes/alcohols/carboxylic acids, characteristics of a homologous series, isomers of C₄H₁₀ and C₄H₈, saturated vs unsaturated, classify alcohol/ether/phenol. ══ 13.1 Organic compounds and catenation (pp. 178–179) ══
Organic chemistry is the study of carbon-containing compounds (hydrocarbons and their derivatives) and their properties. CO, CO₂, carbonates and carbides are treated as inorganic because their properties are very different.
Organic compounds contain carbon combined mainly with H, O, N, S, P and halogens. They are found in living things (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, DNA) and in everyday products: plastics, rubber, synthetic fibres, paints, glues, medicines, dyes, soaps, detergents, fuels (coal, petroleum, natural gas).
Why are there millions of organic compounds? Catenation: carbon atoms can link to each other by strong covalent bonds to form long chains, branched chains and rings. This self-linking ability is called catenation. Carbon also forms four bonds (tetravalency) and can form single, double and triple bonds, and bonds with many other elements.
نامیاتی کیمیا کاربن کے مرکبات کا علم ہے۔ کاربن کے ایٹم آپس میں جڑ کر لمبی زنجیریں، شاخیں اور حلقے بنا سکتے ہیں؛ اس صلاحیت کو کیٹی نیشن کہتے ہیں۔ اسی وجہ سے لاکھوں نامیاتی مرکبات موجود ہیں۔

══ 13.2 Straight-chain, branched-chain and cyclic compounds (pp. 182–183) ══
Organic compounds are classified by the shape of their carbon skeleton:
1. Open-chain (acyclic) compounds – carbon atoms form chains, not rings.
- Straight-chain: carbon atoms joined one after another in a single continuous chain, e.g. butane CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃, n-pentane.
- Branched-chain: one or more carbon atoms (side groups) are attached to the side of the main chain, e.g. 2-methylpropane (isobutane) CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₃.
2. Closed-chain (cyclic) compounds – atoms form one or more rings.
- Homocyclic (carbocyclic): the ring contains only carbon atoms, e.g. cyclohexane, benzene C₆H₆.
- Heterocyclic: the ring contains at least one atom other than carbon (N, O, S), e.g. pyridine, furan.
[Table: Classification by carbon skeleton]
Type | Feature | Example
• Straight-chain | Continuous unbranched chain | CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (butane)
• Branched-chain | Side carbon groups on the chain | CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃ (2-methylpropane)
• Homocyclic (carbocyclic) | Ring of carbon atoms only | Cyclohexane C₆H₁₂, benzene C₆H₆
• Heterocyclic | Ring includes N, O or S | Pyridine C₅H₅N, furan C₄H₄O
کھلی زنجیر والے مرکبات سیدھی (بیوٹین) یا شاخ دار (2-میتھائل پروپین) ہوتے ہیں۔ بند زنجیر یعنی حلقہ دار مرکبات میں ایٹم حلقہ بناتے ہیں؛ اگر حلقے میں صرف کاربن ہو تو ہوموسائیکلک (بینزین) اور اگر کوئی دوسرا ایٹم بھی ہو تو ہیٹروسائیکلک۔

══ 13.3 Molecular, structural and condensed formulae (pp. 180–182) ══
- Molecular formula: the number of each kind of atom: C₄H₁₀.
- Structural (displayed) formula: an unambiguous drawing showing how all atoms are arranged and bonded, with every bond drawn as a line. Two compounds can have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae, e.g. C₂H₆O is ethanol CH₃–CH₂–OH (O bonded to one C and one H) or dimethyl ether CH₃–O–CH₃ (O bonded to two C).
- Condensed structural formula: a shorter form listing each carbon with its hydrogens in order: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ or CH₃(CH₂)₂CH₃.
Drawing alkanes (e.g. pentane): “pent” = 5 carbons; “-ane” = alkane. Draw a chain of 5 C; add H so each C has 4 bonds (3 H on end carbons, 2 H on middle carbons). Condensed: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃. Molecular: C₅H₁₂ (from CₙH₂ₙ₊₂).
Every carbon must have 4 bonds, oxygen 2, nitrogen 3, hydrogen and halogens 1.
[Table: Table 13.2 – Straight-chain alkanes]
Name | Molecular formula | Condensed formula
• Methane | CH₄ | CH₄
• Ethane | C₂H₆ | CH₃CH₃
• Propane | C₃H₈ | CH₃CH₂CH₃
• Butane | C₄H₁₀ | CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃
• Pentane | C₅H₁₂ | CH₃(CH₂)₃CH₃
• Hexane | C₆H₁₄ | CH₃(CH₂)₄CH₃
• Heptane | C₇H₁₆ | CH₃(CH₂)₅CH₃
• Octane | C₈H₁₈ | CH₃(CH₂)₆CH₃
• Nonane | C₉H₂₀ | CH₃(CH₂)₇CH₃
• Decane | C₁₀H₂₂ | CH₃(CH₂)₈CH₃
مالیکیولر فارمولا صرف ایٹموں کی تعداد بتاتا ہے، ساختی فارمولا ہر ایٹم اور بانڈ کی ترتیب واضح دکھاتا ہے، اور مختصر ساختی فارمولا جیسے CH₃CH₂CH₃ ہر کاربن کے ساتھ اس کے ہائیڈروجن لکھتا ہے۔ ہر کاربن کے چار بانڈ ہونے چاہییں۔

══ 13.4 Homologous series and general formulae (pp. 179–180) ══
A homologous series is a family of organic compounds in which adjacent members differ by a –CH₂– unit and which have the same functional group.
General characteristics:
1. Same functional group.
2. Same general formula.
3. Successive members differ by –CH₂– (14 mass units).
4. Gradual trend in physical properties – boiling point, melting point and density increase as the chain gets longer (more intermolecular forces).
5. Similar chemical properties (because of the same functional group).
6. Can be prepared by similar methods.
[Table: Table 13.1 – General formulae]
Homologous series | General formula | First members
• Alkanes | CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ | CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈
• Alkenes | CₙH₂ₙ | C₂H₄, C₃H₆, C₄H₈
• Alkynes | CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ | C₂H₂, C₃H₄, C₄H₆
• Alcohols | CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH | CH₃OH, C₂H₅OH, C₃H₇OH
• Carboxylic acids | CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH (R–COOH) | HCOOH (n = 0), CH₃COOH, C₂H₅COOH
• Aldehydes | R–CHO | HCHO, CH₃CHO
• Ketones | R–CO–R′ | CH₃COCH₃
Exam Tip: Using a general formula: alkene with 3 C → C₃H₆; alkyne with 4 C → C₄H₆; alcohol with 2 C → C₂H₅OH; alkane with 5 C → C₅H₁₂.
ہم جنس سلسلہ نامیاتی مرکبات کا ایسا خاندان ہے جس کے ساتھ والے ارکان میں CH₂ کا فرق ہو، فنکشنل گروپ اور عمومی فارمولا ایک ہو، کیمیائی خصوصیات ملتی جلتی ہوں اور طبعی خصوصیات (نقطہ ابال وغیرہ) بتدریج بدلیں۔ الکین CₙH₂ₙ₊₂، الکین (ڈبل بانڈ) CₙH₂ₙ، الکائن CₙH₂ₙ₋₂، الکحل CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH۔

══ 13.5 Saturated and unsaturated compounds (pp. 184) ══
- Saturated compounds: all carbon–carbon bonds are single bonds (C–C). They contain the maximum possible number of hydrogens. Alkanes (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂) are saturated hydrocarbons: methane, ethane, propane, butane.
- Unsaturated compounds: contain one or more C=C double bonds or C≡C triple bonds.
- Alkenes (CₙH₂ₙ): at least one C=C, e.g. ethene CH₂=CH₂, propene CH₃CH=CH₂.
- Alkynes (CₙH₂ₙ₋₂): at least one C≡C, e.g. ethyne HC≡CH.
Unsaturated compounds can add hydrogen (or other atoms) across the multiple bond (addition reactions); saturated compounds undergo substitution.
Alkene vs alkyne: alkene has a C=C double bond and formula CₙH₂ₙ; alkyne has a C≡C triple bond and formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
سیر شدہ مرکبات میں تمام کاربن کاربن بانڈ سنگل ہوتے ہیں (الکینز جیسے میتھین)۔ غیر سیر شدہ مرکبات میں کم از کم ایک ڈبل (الکین) یا ٹرپل (الکائن) بانڈ ہوتا ہے جیسے ایتھین CH₂=CH₂ اور ایتھائن HC≡CH۔

══ 13.6 Structural isomerism (pp. 183–184) ══
Structural isomers are compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae (different arrangement of atoms). The phenomenon is isomerism. Isomers have different physical (and sometimes chemical) properties.
C₄H₁₀ (two isomers – chain isomers):
- Butane (n-butane): CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃ (straight chain), b.p. −0.5 °C
- 2-Methylpropane (isobutane): CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₃ (branched), b.p. −12 °C
C₄H₈ (alkene position isomers):
- But-1-ene: CH₃–CH₂–CH=CH₂ (double bond at the end)
- But-2-ene: CH₃–CH=CH–CH₃ (double bond in the middle)
(2-methylpropene (CH₃)₂C=CH₂ is a third C₄H₈ isomer.)
C₂H₆O: ethanol CH₃CH₂OH (alcohol) and dimethyl ether CH₃OCH₃ (ether) – functional-group isomers.
C₃H₆O₂: propanoic acid CH₃CH₂COOH and methyl ethanoate CH₃COOCH₃.
CH₄, C₂H₆ and C₃H₈ have no structural isomers – there is only one way to arrange their atoms. Isomerism starts with C₄H₁₀.
Exam Tip: To check whether two formulae are isomers: count atoms (must be identical), then check whether the bonding arrangement is really different (simply bending or flipping the chain does not make a new isomer).
ساختی آئسومرز وہ مرکبات ہیں جن کا مالیکیولر فارمولا ایک مگر ساختی فارمولا مختلف ہو۔ C₄H₁₀ کے دو آئسومر: بیوٹین (سیدھی زنجیر) اور 2-میتھائل پروپین (شاخ دار)۔ C₄H₈: بیوٹ-1-این اور بیوٹ-2-این۔

══ 13.7 Functional groups (pp. 182–190) ══
A functional group is an atom or group of atoms in a molecule that determines the chemical properties of a homologous series. It is the reactive site; it is used to classify and name compounds. The rest of the molecule is usually an alkyl group R (CH₃–, C₂H₅–).
- Haloalkanes: –X (F, Cl, Br, I), R–X, e.g. CH₃Cl chloromethane.
- Alcohols: hydroxyl group –OH attached to an alkyl chain, R–OH: methanol CH₃OH (poisonous, causes blindness), ethanol C₂H₅OH.
- Phenols: –OH attached directly to a benzene ring, C₆H₅OH (first antiseptic; strong germicide/disinfectant).
- Ethers: C–O–C linkage, R–O–R′: dimethyl ether CH₃OCH₃, diethyl ether C₂H₅OC₂H₅ (old anaesthetic).
- Aldehydes: carbonyl group with at least one H, –CHO, R–CHO: methanal (formaldehyde) HCHO, ethanal (acetaldehyde) CH₃CHO.
- Ketones: carbonyl group between two alkyl groups, R–CO–R′: propanone (acetone) CH₃COCH₃ (nail-polish remover), butanone.
- Carboxylic acids: carboxyl group –COOH, R–COOH: methanoic (formic) acid HCOOH, ethanoic (acetic) acid CH₃COOH.
- Esters: –COO– (R–COO–R′): methyl ethanoate CH₃COOCH₃, ethyl ethanoate CH₃COOC₂H₅ (fruity smells).
- Amines: amino group –NH₂, R–NH₂: methylamine CH₃NH₂, ethylamine.
- Amides: –CONH₂, R–CO–NH₂: ethanamide CH₃CONH₂.
Carbonyl vs carboxyl: carbonyl is C=O (aldehydes, ketones); carboxyl is –COOH (C=O plus –OH on the same carbon).
[Table: Table 13.3 – Common functional groups]
Class | Functional group | General formula | Example
• Alkane | none (C–C, C–H) | R–H | CH₄ methane
• Alkene | C=C | R–CH=CH₂ | CH₂=CH₂ ethene
• Alkyne | C≡C | R–C≡C–R′ | HC≡CH ethyne
• Haloalkane | –X | R–X | CH₃Cl
• Alcohol | –OH | R–OH | C₂H₅OH ethanol
• Phenol | –OH on benzene ring | Ar–OH | C₆H₅OH
• Ether | –O– | R–O–R′ | CH₃OCH₃
• Aldehyde | –CHO | R–CHO | CH₃CHO ethanal
• Ketone | >C=O | R–CO–R′ | CH₃COCH₃ propanone
• Carboxylic acid | –COOH | R–COOH | CH₃COOH ethanoic acid
• Ester | –COO– | R–COO–R′ | CH₃COOCH₃
• Amine | –NH₂ | R–NH₂ | CH₃NH₂
• Amide | –CONH₂ | R–CONH₂ | CH₃CONH₂
Exam Tip: Classify alcohol/ether/phenol: –OH on an alkyl group = alcohol; –OH on a benzene ring = phenol; O between two alkyl groups = ether.
فنکشنل گروپ ایٹم یا ایٹموں کا وہ گروہ ہے جو کسی ہم جنس سلسلے کی کیمیائی خصوصیات طے کرتا ہے: الکحل (–OH)، فینول (بینزین پر –OH)، ایتھر (–O–)، ایلڈی ہائیڈ (–CHO)، کیٹون (R–CO–R′)، کاربوکسلک ایسڈ (–COOH)، ایسٹر (–COO–)، امین (–NH₂) اور امائیڈ (–CONH₂)۔

══ KEY DIAGRAMS & FIGURES ══
1. Isomers of C₄H₁₀ and C₄H₈: Same molecular formula, different arrangement of atoms.
chapters.shortNotes:
══ Chapter 13 in one page
- Organic chemistry: carbon compounds (not CO, CO₂, carbonates, carbides). Catenation → chains, branches, rings.
- Skeletons: straight-chain (butane), branched (2-methylpropane), cyclic: homocyclic (benzene, cyclohexane), heterocyclic (pyridine).
- Formulae: molecular (C₄H₁₀), structural (all bonds shown), condensed (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃). Stems: meth 1 … dec 10.
- Homologous series: same functional group and general formula; differ by –CH₂–; gradual physical trend; similar chemistry. Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; alkenes CₙH₂ₙ; alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂; alcohols CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH; acids CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH.
- Saturated = only C–C single bonds (alkanes). Unsaturated = C=C or C≡C (alkenes, alkynes).
- Structural isomers: same molecular, different structural formula. C₄H₁₀: butane, 2-methylpropane. C₄H₈: but-1-ene, but-2-ene. C₂H₆O: ethanol, dimethyl ether.
- Functional groups: –OH alcohol; Ar–OH phenol; –O– ether; –CHO aldehyde; R–CO–R′ ketone; –COOH acid; –COO– ester; –NH₂ amine; –CONH₂ amide; –X haloalkane.

chapters.definitions:
• Organic chemistry (نامیاتی کیمیا) [p. 178]: The study of carbon-containing compounds (hydrocarbons and their derivatives) and their properties.
• Catenation (زنجیر سازی) [p. 183]: The ability of carbon atoms to link with one another to form long chains, branched chains and rings.
• Hydrocarbon (ہائیڈروکاربن) [p. 184]: A compound containing only carbon and hydrogen.
• Structural formula (ساختی فارمولا) [p. 180]: A formula that shows unambiguously how the atoms in a molecule are arranged and bonded.
• Condensed structural formula (مختصر ساختی فارمولا) [p. 180]: A shortened structural formula listing each carbon with its attached atoms in order, e.g. CH₃CH₂CH₃.
• Homologous series (ہم جنس سلسلہ) [p. 179]: A family of organic compounds with the same functional group and general formula, in which adjacent members differ by –CH₂–.
• Functional group (فنکشنل گروپ) [p. 182]: An atom or group of atoms that determines the chemical properties of a homologous series.
• Saturated compound (سیر شدہ مرکب) [p. 184]: A compound whose molecules contain only single carbon–carbon bonds.
• Unsaturated compound (غیر سیر شدہ مرکب) [p. 184]: A compound whose molecules contain one or more carbon–carbon double or triple bonds.
• Structural isomers (ساختی آئسومرز) [p. 183]: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.
• Straight-chain compound (سیدھی زنجیر والا مرکب) [p. 182]: An open-chain compound with carbon atoms in one continuous unbranched chain.
• Branched-chain compound (شاخ دار مرکب) [p. 183]: An open-chain compound with carbon side groups attached to the main chain.
• Cyclic compound (حلقہ دار مرکب) [p. 183]: A compound in which atoms form one or more rings.
• Heterocyclic compound (ہیٹروسائیکلک مرکب) [p. 183]: A cyclic compound whose ring contains at least one atom other than carbon.
• Alkyl group (R) (الکائل گروپ) [p. 182]: A group formed by removing one H from an alkane, e.g. CH₃– (methyl), C₂H₅– (ethyl).

══ BILINGUAL GLOSSARY ══
• Organic (نامیاتی): Carbon-based
• Catenation (زنجیر سازی): Carbon–carbon linking
• Hydrocarbon (ہائیڈروکاربن): Only C and H
• Homologous series (ہم جنس سلسلہ): Family differing by CH₂
• Functional group (فعالی گروہ): Reactive group
• Isomer (ہم ترکیب): Same formula, different structure
• Saturated (سیر شدہ): Single bonds only
• Unsaturated (غیر سیر شدہ): Has double/triple bonds
• Alkyl group (الکائل گروہ): R group, e.g. CH₃–
• Cyclic (حلقہ دار): Ring-shaped
• Branched (شاخ دار): With side chains
• Carbonyl (کاربونیل): C=O group
chapters.formulasAndConcepts:
══ KEY FORMULAS & QUANTITIES ══
• Alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (Saturated)
• Alkenes: CₙH₂ₙ (One C=C)
• Alkynes: CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (One C≡C)
• Alcohols: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH (R–OH)
• Carboxylic acids: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH (R–COOH)
• Aldehydes: R–CHO
• Ketones: R–CO–R′
• Ethers: R–O–R′
• Esters: R–COO–R′
• Amines: R–NH₂
• Amides: R–CONH₂
• Difference between homologues: –CH₂– (14 amu)

══ KEY EQUATIONS & DERIVATIONS ══
• CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O -> CH₃CH₂OH — Hydration of ethene: alkene (C=C) becomes alcohol (–OH) (review Q19).
• CH₂=CHCl -> polymerisation -> PVC — Vinyl chloride (unsaturated) makes polyvinyl chloride.
• C₂H₅OH + CH₃COOH  CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O — Alcohol + carboxylic acid → ester (illustration of functional groups reacting).

══ CONCEPTUAL REASONING (SLO-BASED) ══
1. Why are CO₂ and CaCO₃ not studied as organic compounds even though they contain carbon?
   Answer: Their properties are like inorganic compounds (no C–H bonds or carbon chains).
2. Why do boiling points increase along a homologous series?
   Answer: Each extra –CH₂– makes the molecule larger, so intermolecular forces become stronger and more energy is needed to separate molecules.
3. Can C₃H₈ have isomers?
   Answer: No. Three carbons can be joined in only one way.
4. Why is phenol not classified as an alcohol?
   Answer: Its –OH is attached directly to a benzene ring, which changes its properties (phenol is weakly acidic).

══ APPLIED & REAL-LIFE CONCEPTS ══
1. Nail-polish remover smells sweet and evaporates quickly. Its main component is CH₃COCH₃. Which class does it belong to?
   Answer: Ketone (propanone / acetone).
2. Vinegar is about 5% of a compound with formula CH₃COOH. Name it and its functional group.
   Answer: Ethanoic (acetic) acid; carboxyl group –COOH.
3. Why is methanol dangerous to drink while ethanol is used in medicines?
   Answer: Methanol is converted in the body to toxic products (formaldehyde, formic acid) causing blindness or death.
chapters.solvedExamples:
══ WORKED TEXTBOOK EXAMPLES ══

1. Give the molecular, structural and condensed formulae for pentane. (Example 13.1)
   Solution: “Pent” = 5 C, “-ane” = alkane. Structural: a chain of five C atoms; the two end carbons each carry 3 H and the three middle carbons carry 2 H each, all bonds single. Condensed: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃. Molecular: C₅H₁₂ (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ with n = 5).

2. Write the molecular formulae using general formulae: alkane with 6 C; alkene with 4 C; alkyne with 3 C; alcohol with 3 C.
   Solution: Alkane C₆H₁₄; alkene C₄H₈; alkyne C₃H₄; alcohol C₃H₇OH.

3. Classify as alcohol, ether or phenol: (1) CH₃CH₂OCH₂CH₃ (2) C₆H₅OH (3) CH₃OH. (Example 13.3)
   Solution: (1) Ether – O between two alkyl groups (diethyl ether, old anaesthetic). (2) Phenol – OH on benzene ring (germicide). (3) Alcohol – OH on an alkyl group (methanol, poisonous).
chapters.solvedExercises:
NBF Chapter 13 Exercises (192–194):

— Exercise MCQs —
i. Condensed structural formula for butane is: → B (CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃) | Butane has 4 carbons.
ii. CH₃–CH₂–CH₃ is the chemical formula for: → B (Propane) | 3 carbons = propane.
iii. Which compound is not a saturated hydrocarbon? → C (CH₃–CH=CH₂) | Propene has a C=C double bond.
iv. Stem “But” stands for how many carbon atoms? → C (4) | But- = 4.
v. The functional group –C(=O)– (carbonyl between two carbons) is found in: → B (Ketones) | Ketones contain C=O bonded to two alkyl groups.
vi. In which compound is oxygen attached to two alkyl carbon atoms? → C (Ether) | R–O–R′.
vii. Which of the following is an alcohol? → D (CH₃–CH₂–OH) | Ethanol: –OH on an alkyl chain. (C₆H₅OH is a phenol.)
viii. The functional group of amines is: → C (–NH₂) | Amino group.
ix. Ethanoic acid contains the functional group: → C (–COOH) | Carboxyl group.

— Q2. Give short answers —
(—) What is catenation?
   Answer: The ability of carbon atoms to link with each other by covalent bonds to form long chains, branched chains and rings. It is the main reason for the huge number of organic compounds.
(i) Define isomerism.
   Answer: The existence of two or more compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae (arrangements of atoms), e.g. butane and 2-methylpropane (C₄H₁₀).
(ii) Give three examples of unsaturated compounds.
   Answer: Ethene CH₂=CH₂, propene CH₃CH=CH₂, ethyne HC≡CH (also but-1-ene, vinyl chloride).
(iii) Define a functional group.
   Answer: An atom or group of atoms in an organic molecule that determines the characteristic chemical properties of the compound and its homologous series, e.g. –OH, –COOH, –CHO.
(iv) What is the difference between an alkene and an alkyne?
   Answer: An alkene has at least one C=C double bond and general formula CₙH₂ₙ (ethene). An alkyne has at least one C≡C triple bond and general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (ethyne).

— Q3–Q19. Descriptive questions —
3. Identify the compounds on the basis of functional groups and show the functional group: CH₃–CH=CH₂; CH₃–CH₂–COOH; CH₃–CO–OH; CH₃–CO–CH₃; CH₃–CO–OCH₃; H–CO–CH₃.
   Answer: - CH₃–CH=CH₂: alkene (C=C) – propene
- CH₃–CH₂–COOH: carboxylic acid (–COOH) – propanoic acid
- CH₃–CO–OH (CH₃COOH): carboxylic acid (–COOH) – ethanoic acid
- CH₃–CO–CH₃: ketone (C=O between two carbons) – propanone
- CH₃–CO–OCH₃: ester (–COO–) – methyl ethanoate
- H–CO–CH₃ (CH₃CHO): aldehyde (–CHO) – ethanal
4. What is the name of the alkane having four carbon atoms in the chain?
   Answer: Butane, C₄H₁₀ (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃).
5. Give the structural formulae of two simple alkanes and one alkyne.
   Answer: Methane: C with four H (CH₄). Ethane: H₃C–CH₃ (two C each with three H). Ethyne: H–C≡C–H.
6. What is meant by the term functional group?
   Answer: The atom or group of atoms that is the reactive part of an organic molecule and decides its chemical properties; compounds with the same functional group belong to the same class/homologous series (e.g. all alcohols have –OH).
7. Identify as alcohol, aldehyde or ketone: (a) HCHO (used to make polymers and urotropine) (b) CH₃COCH₃ (nail polish remover) (c) CH₃CH₂OH (used in plastics, cosmetics, tinctures)
   Answer: (a) Aldehyde – methanal (formaldehyde). (b) Ketone – propanone (acetone). (c) Alcohol – ethanol.
8. Give the molecular formula of a compound containing C, H and O with single bonds only. List all the possible functional groups it can have.
   Answer: Example C₂H₆O. With only single bonds the oxygen can be in an alcohol (–OH): CH₃CH₂OH (ethanol), or an ether (C–O–C): CH₃OCH₃ (dimethyl ether). (Aldehydes, ketones, acids and esters need C=O double bonds, so they are not possible.)
9. Give condensed structural formulae of the compounds shown and classify them: (a) H–C–C–C–OH (three C in a chain with H) (b) H₃C–O–CH₃
   Answer: (a) CH₃CH₂CH₂OH – propan-1-ol, an alcohol. (b) CH₃OCH₃ – dimethyl ether, an ether.
10. The diagram (X–Y(X₂)–Y(X₂)–Z–X) shows an organic compound with three different elements. Select the possible compound: ethanoic acid, propene, ethanol, propane.
   Answer: Y has four bonds (carbon), X has one bond (hydrogen), Z has two bonds (oxygen): H–C(H₂)–C(H₂)–O–H = ethanol, C₂H₅OH.
11. PVC is made from vinyl chloride CH₂=CHCl. Classify vinyl chloride as saturated or unsaturated.
   Answer: Unsaturated – it contains a C=C double bond (that is why it can polymerise to PVC).
12. Sketch the structural formula of a two-carbon compound containing: (a) alcohol (b) aldehyde (c) carboxylic acid (d) alkene.
   Answer: (a) Ethanol CH₃–CH₂–OH (b) Ethanal CH₃–CHO (C=O with H on the end carbon) (c) Ethanoic acid CH₃–COOH (d) Ethene CH₂=CH₂.
13. Aspirin is made from salicylic acid (benzene ring with –COOH and –OH). Select the functional groups present and justify.
   Answer: Carboxylic acid (–COOH) – C=O and –OH on the same carbon; phenol (–OH on the benzene ring) – the –OH is attached directly to the ring, not to an alkyl chain, so it is a phenolic group, not an alcohol.
18. Construct the general formula for an alkane, alkene, alkyne and alcohol containing 4 carbon atoms.
   Answer: Alkane C₄H₁₀; alkene C₄H₈; alkyne C₄H₆; alcohol C₄H₉OH.
19. Water adds to ethene: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O → CH₃CH₂OH. Compare the functional groups in reactant and product.
   Answer: Reactant ethene has a C=C double bond (alkene, unsaturated). Product ethanol has the –OH group (alcohol) and only single C–C bonds (saturated). Water adds H to one carbon and OH to the other across the double bond.
chapters.importantQuestions:
══ SHORT RESPONSE QUESTIONS (PAST PAPERS, MODEL PAPERS & SLO PRACTICE) ══

1. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] What is meant by molecular formula and structural formula? Give one example each. Show that C₃H₆O₂ can have more than one structural formula.
   Answer: Molecular formula: number of atoms of each element – C₃H₆O₂. Structural formula: arrangement and bonding of atoms. C₃H₆O₂ can be propanoic acid CH₃CH₂COOH or methyl ethanoate CH₃COOCH₃ (or ethyl methanoate HCOOC₂H₅).

2. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] Classify as alcohol, ether or phenol: CH₃OCH₂CH₃, CH₃OH, C₆H₅OH.
   Answer: CH₃OCH₂CH₃ – ether; CH₃OH – alcohol; C₆H₅OH – phenol.

3. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] What is meant by a homologous series in organic chemistry? Why do members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties?
   Answer: A family of compounds with the same functional group and general formula in which adjacent members differ by –CH₂–. They have similar chemical properties because they contain the same functional group, which is the reactive part of the molecule.

4. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] Draw the structural formula of ethene (C₂H₄) and ethanol (C₂H₅OH) showing the correct bonds.
   Answer: Ethene: H₂C=CH₂ (each C bonded to 2 H and doubly bonded to the other C). Ethanol: H₃C–CH₂–O–H (all single bonds; each C has 4 bonds; O has 2).

5. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] Write any three characteristics of a homologous series.
   Answer: Same functional group; same general formula; successive members differ by –CH₂–; gradual change in physical properties; similar chemical properties (any three).

6. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026 (Old-22)] Draw the structural formula of CH₃OH and identify its functional group.
   Answer: H₃C–O–H (C bonded to 3 H and to O; O bonded to H). Functional group: hydroxyl, –OH (alcohol).

7. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026 (Old-22)] Draw the different possible correct structural formulae of (a) C₄H₁₀ (b) C₄H₈.
   Answer: (a) CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (butane) and CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃ (2-methylpropane). (b) CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂ (but-1-ene), CH₃CH=CHCH₃ (but-2-ene) and (CH₃)₂C=CH₂ (2-methylpropene).

8. [Verified Official - FBISE 2nd Annual 2025] Draw the structural formula of C₄H₁₀. Is it saturated or unsaturated?
   Answer: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃ (or the branched isomer). It is saturated – only single C–C bonds.

9. [Verified Official - FBISE 2nd Annual 2025] Compare aldehydes and ketones. Give one example of each.
   Answer: Both contain the carbonyl group C=O. In aldehydes the carbonyl carbon is bonded to at least one H (–CHO), e.g. ethanal CH₃CHO. In ketones it is bonded to two alkyl groups (R–CO–R′), e.g. propanone CH₃COCH₃.

10. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] Draw structural formulae of (a) methanol (b) methanoic acid.
   Answer: (a) CH₃–OH (b) H–COOH (H–C(=O)–O–H).

11. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] Write general formulae with one example each: alkene, alkyne, alcohol.
   Answer: Alkene CₙH₂ₙ – ethene C₂H₄; alkyne CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ – ethyne C₂H₂; alcohol CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH – ethanol C₂H₅OH.

12. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] Draw structural formulae of (a) methanoic acid (b) propane.
   Answer: (a) H–COOH (b) CH₃–CH₂–CH₃.

13. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] Write general formulae with one example: alkene, carboxylic acid, alkane.
   Answer: Alkene CₙH₂ₙ (C₂H₄); carboxylic acid CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH (CH₃COOH); alkane CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (CH₄).

14. [Verified Official - FBISE Model Paper (AF and 50%)] Identify the functional groups in (a) CH₃COOH (b) CH₃CHO (c) CH₃CH₂OH.
   Answer: (a) –COOH carboxyl (carboxylic acid) (b) –CHO aldehyde group (c) –OH hydroxyl (alcohol).


══ EXTENDED / LONG RESPONSE QUESTIONS ══

1. Describe organic compounds as straight-chain, branched-chain and cyclic, with examples.
   Answer: Open-chain: straight (butane CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃) or branched (2-methylpropane CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃). Cyclic: homocyclic/carbocyclic with only C in the ring (cyclohexane, benzene) or heterocyclic with N, O or S in the ring (pyridine, furan). Catenation allows carbon to form all these skeletons.

2. Define structural isomers. Draw and name the isomers of C₄H₁₀ and C₄H₈.
   Answer: Same molecular formula, different structural formula. C₄H₁₀: butane CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ and 2-methylpropane CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃. C₄H₈: but-1-ene CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂ and but-2-ene CH₃CH=CHCH₃ (also 2-methylpropene).

3. What is a functional group? Write the functional groups and one example each of alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters and amines.
   Answer: Functional group: atom/group of atoms that determines the properties of a class of compounds. Alcohol –OH (ethanol); aldehyde –CHO (ethanal); ketone R–CO–R′ (propanone); carboxylic acid –COOH (ethanoic acid); ester –COO– (ethyl ethanoate); amine –NH₂ (methylamine). (Also phenol C₆H₅OH, ether –O–, amide –CONH₂.)
chapters.chapterSummary:
══ Chapter 13 in one page
- Organic chemistry: carbon compounds (not CO, CO₂, carbonates, carbides). Catenation → chains, branches, rings.
- Skeletons: straight-chain (butane), branched (2-methylpropane), cyclic: homocyclic (benzene, cyclohexane), heterocyclic (pyridine).
- Formulae: molecular (C₄H₁₀), structural (all bonds shown), condensed (CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃). Stems: meth 1 … dec 10.
- Homologous series: same functional group and general formula; differ by –CH₂–; gradual physical trend; similar chemistry. Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂; alkenes CₙH₂ₙ; alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂; alcohols CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH; acids CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH.
- Saturated = only C–C single bonds (alkanes). Unsaturated = C=C or C≡C (alkenes, alkynes).
- Structural isomers: same molecular, different structural formula. C₄H₁₀: butane, 2-methylpropane. C₄H₈: but-1-ene, but-2-ene. C₂H₆O: ethanol, dimethyl ether.
- Functional groups: –OH alcohol; Ar–OH phenol; –O– ether; –CHO aldehyde; R–CO–R′ ketone; –COOH acid; –COO– ester; –NH₂ amine; –CONH₂ amide; –X haloalkane.

کاربن کی زنجیر سازی سے لاکھوں مرکبات بنتے ہیں۔ ہم جنس سلسلے میں CH₂ کا فرق اور ایک ہی فنکشنل گروپ ہوتا ہے۔ سیر شدہ میں صرف سنگل بانڈ، غیر سیر شدہ میں ڈبل یا ٹرپل۔ آئسومرز: ایک فارمولا، مختلف ساخت۔ فنکشنل گروپس: –OH، –CHO، –CO–، –COOH، –COO–، –NH₂۔

chapters.title: Hydrocarbons
chapters.introduction:
Hydrocarbons are the simplest organic compounds – they contain only carbon and hydrogen. This short unit focuses on alkanes, the saturated hydrocarbons: their single covalent bonds, how they are prepared (hydrogenation of alkenes and alkynes, reduction of alkyl halides, cracking of large hydrocarbons), their physical properties, and their two important reactions: combustion and substitution by chlorine in light.

A small chapter that is asked in almost every paper: preparation of ethane/propane/methane with equations, substitution of methane with Cl₂ (diffused vs direct sunlight), complete vs incomplete combustion of methane, why alkanes are unreactive, and conditions for hydrogenation (Ni, 200–300 °C) and cracking (450–750 °C).

══ FBISE ASSESSMENT & EXAM WEIGHTAGE ══
A small chapter that is asked in almost every paper: preparation of ethane/propane/methane with equations, substitution of methane with Cl₂ (diffused vs direct sunlight), complete vs incomplete combustion of methane, why alkanes are unreactive, and conditions for hydrogenation (Ni, 200–300 °C) and cracking (450–750 °C).
Note: Textbook printing errors corrected here: the general formula of alkanes is printed garbled (it is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂), and the methane combustion equation is printed as “CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂ + heat” (the product is 2H₂O).

══ 14.1 Alkanes: saturated hydrocarbons with single covalent bonds (pp. 196) ══
Hydrocarbons are compounds containing only carbon and hydrogen. They are classified by the type of carbon–carbon bond: alkanes (C–C), alkenes (C=C), alkynes (C≡C).
Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons: every carbon–carbon bond is a single covalent bond, and each carbon forms four single bonds (tetrahedral). General formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
- Methane CH₄ – simplest alkane; main component of natural gas (Sui gas). Each of carbon's four outer electrons pairs with one electron from a hydrogen atom: four shared pairs (dot-and-cross).
- Ethane C₂H₆ – CH₃–CH₃; one C–C single bond and six C–H bonds.
- Propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀ (LPG).
They are called saturated because each carbon is joined to the maximum number of hydrogen atoms – no more H can be added.
[Table: First members of the alkanes]
Alkane | Formula | Condensed structure | State (room temp.)
• Methane | CH₄ | CH₄ | Gas
• Ethane | C₂H₆ | CH₃CH₃ | Gas
• Propane | C₃H₈ | CH₃CH₂CH₃ | Gas
• Butane | C₄H₁₀ | CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ | Gas
• Pentane | C₅H₁₂ | CH₃(CH₂)₃CH₃ | Liquid
الکینز سیر شدہ ہائیڈروکاربن ہیں جن میں تمام کاربن کاربن بانڈ سنگل کوویلنٹ ہوتے ہیں۔ عمومی فارمولا CₙH₂ₙ₊₂۔ میتھین CH₄ قدرتی گیس کا بڑا حصہ ہے۔ انہیں سیر شدہ اس لیے کہتے ہیں کہ ہر کاربن زیادہ سے زیادہ ہائیڈروجن ایٹموں سے جڑا ہوتا ہے۔

══ 14.2 Preparation 1: hydrogenation of alkenes and alkynes (pp. 196) ══
Hydrogenation is the addition of hydrogen (H₂) across a carbon–carbon multiple bond.
Conditions: finely divided nickel catalyst at 200–300 °C and high pressure; or platinum (Pt) or palladium (Pd) at room temperature.
- Alkene + 1 H₂ → alkane: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃–CH₃ (ethene → ethane)
- Alkyne + 2 H₂ → alkane: HC≡CH + 2H₂ → CH₃–CH₃ (ethyne → ethane)
An alkyne adds two molecules of hydrogen because its triple bond has two “extra” bonds to open (it goes through the alkene stage: ethyne → ethene → ethane).
Propane: CH₃CH=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃CH₂CH₃; CH₃C≡CH + 2H₂ → CH₃CH₂CH₃.
Industrial use: hydrogenation of vegetable oils makes vegetable ghee/margarine.
ہائیڈروجنیشن: کثیر بانڈ پر ہائیڈروجن کا اضافہ۔ نکل کیٹالسٹ (200–300 °C) یا پلاٹینم/پیلیڈیم کی موجودگی میں۔ ایتھین + H₂ → ایتھین؛ ایتھائن + 2H₂ → ایتھین۔ الکائن دو مالیکیول ہائیڈروجن لیتا ہے کیونکہ اس میں ٹرپل بانڈ ہوتا ہے۔

══ 14.3 Preparation 2: reduction of alkyl halides (pp. 197) ══
An alkyl halide (haloalkane, R–X) is reduced to an alkane by treating it with zinc and an aqueous acid (usually HCl or CH₃COOH).
Zinc reacts with the acid to release atomic (nascent) hydrogen [H], which is very reactive. The nascent hydrogen replaces the halogen with hydrogen. Addition of hydrogen here is called reduction.
Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + 2[H]
- Methane from methyl chloride: CH₃Cl + 2[H] → CH₄ + HCl
- Ethane from ethyl chloride (chloroethane): CH₃CH₂Cl + 2[H] → CH₃CH₃ + HCl
- Propane from propyl chloride: CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl + 2[H] → CH₃CH₂CH₃ + HCl
- Ethane from bromoethane: C₂H₅Br + 2[H] → C₂H₆ + HBr
The alkane formed has the same number of carbon atoms as the alkyl halide.
الکائل ہیلائیڈ کی تخفیف: زنک اور ہائیڈروکلورک ایسڈ سے نومولود ہائیڈروجن [H] بنتی ہے جو ہیلوجن کو ہٹا کر الکین بناتی ہے: CH₃Cl + 2[H] → CH₄ + HCl۔ بننے والے الکین میں کاربن ایٹموں کی تعداد وہی رہتی ہے۔

══ 14.4 Preparation 3: cracking of larger hydrocarbons (pp. 197) ══
Cracking is the breaking of large hydrocarbon (alkane) molecules into smaller, more useful molecules by heat.
Thermal cracking: heating at high temperature (about 450–750 °C) and high pressure. It produces a mixture of smaller alkanes and alkenes. (Catalytic cracking uses a catalyst such as zeolite/alumina at lower temperature.)
Example: decane → octane + ethene
C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄
Other example: C₈H₁₈ → C₆H₁₄ + C₂H₄
Why crack? Crude oil contains too many large molecules; cracking produces more petrol (small alkanes) for fuel and alkenes (ethene, propene) for making plastics.
Check: atoms must balance (C₁₀H₂₂: 10 C, 22 H → 8 + 2 C, 18 + 4 H).
کریکنگ: بڑے ہائیڈروکاربن مالیکیولز کو زیادہ درجہ حرارت (450–750 °C) اور دباؤ پر توڑ کر چھوٹے الکینز اور الکینز (ڈبل بانڈ) بنانا، مثلاً ڈیکین → آکٹین + ایتھین۔ اس سے زیادہ پٹرول اور پلاسٹک کے لیے ایتھین ملتی ہے۔

══ 14.5 Physical properties and low reactivity of alkanes (pp. 197) ══
Physical properties:
- Non-polar molecules; insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents; less dense than water (float).
- C₁–C₄: colourless, odourless gases; C₅–C₁₇: colourless liquids; C₁₈ and above: waxy solids (paraffin wax).
- Boiling points increase with chain length (stronger intermolecular forces).
- Because they are unreactive, liquid alkanes are good solvents, e.g. hexane is used to extract vegetable oils from corn, soybeans and cotton seeds.
Why are alkanes generally unreactive?
1. All bonds are strong single covalent C–C and C–H bonds (σ bonds) that need a lot of energy to break.
2. C–H bonds are almost non-polar (C and H have similar electronegativity), so there are no charged sites to attract acids, bases or other ionic reagents.
3. They are saturated – no double bond for addition.
So alkanes do not react with acids, alkalis or most oxidising agents. Their important reactions are only combustion and substitution with halogens in light.
الکینز پانی میں حل نہیں ہوتے اور پانی سے ہلکے ہیں۔ C₁–C₄ گیس، C₅–C₁₇ مائع اور اس سے بڑے ٹھوس۔ یہ عام طور پر غیر متعامل ہیں کیونکہ ان کے C–C اور C–H بانڈ مضبوط اور تقریباً غیر قطبی ہیں اور یہ سیر شدہ ہیں۔ ان کے اہم تعاملات صرف احتراق اور ہیلوجن کے ساتھ بدل ہیں۔

══ 14.6 Substitution reaction with chlorine (photochemical) (pp. 197–198) ══
A substitution reaction is one in which one atom or group of atoms in a molecule is replaced by another atom or group of atoms.
Alkanes react with chlorine (or bromine) in the presence of light – a photochemical reaction (a reaction that takes place in the presence of light). One H atom of the alkane is replaced by a Cl atom.
Diffused sunlight / UV light – mono-substitution:
CH₄ + Cl₂ --light--> CH₃Cl + HCl (chloromethane)
Displayed formula of chloromethane: a carbon bonded to three H atoms and one Cl atom.
Ethane: C₂H₆ + Cl₂ --light--> C₂H₅Cl + HCl (chloroethane)
Direct (bright) sunlight: the reaction is explosive and carbon is formed:
CH₄ + 2Cl₂ --direct sunlight--> C + 4HCl
With excess chlorine, further substitution gives CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃ and CCl₄ (beyond the syllabus limit of mono-substitution).
Why substitution? Alkanes are saturated, so they cannot add atoms; the only way to react with chlorine is to swap an H for a Cl. In the dark, no reaction occurs: light provides energy to split Cl₂ into reactive chlorine atoms.
Exam Tip: Exam favourite: write methane + chlorine in (a) diffused sunlight → CH₃Cl + HCl and (b) direct sunlight → C + 4HCl.
بدل کا تعامل: مالیکیول میں ایک ایٹم یا گروپ کی جگہ دوسرا ایٹم یا گروپ آ جانا۔ روشنی میں میتھین اور کلورین: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (کلورومیتھین)۔ براہ راست دھوپ میں تعامل دھماکہ خیز ہوتا ہے: CH₄ + 2Cl₂ → C + 4HCl۔ الکینز سیر شدہ ہیں اس لیے صرف بدل کا تعامل کرتے ہیں۔

══ 14.7 Combustion of alkanes (pp. 198) ══
Combustion is the reaction of a substance with oxygen (air) that rapidly releases heat and produces a flame. It is exothermic.
Complete combustion (excess oxygen): gives carbon dioxide, water and heat; most alkanes burn with a blue flame.
CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat
C₂H₆: 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O + heat
C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O + heat
Incomplete combustion (limited oxygen): gives carbon monoxide (CO) and/or carbon (soot) and water; yellow, sooty flame; less heat. CO is a poisonous gas.
2CH₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO + 4H₂O
CH₄ + O₂ → C + 2H₂O
Why lighter alkanes are used as fuels: (i) their combustion can be controlled, (ii) they release a large amount of heat per gram, (iii) they are cheap and readily available (natural gas, LPG, petrol).
[Table: Complete vs incomplete combustion]
 | Complete | Incomplete
• Oxygen supply | Excess / plenty | Limited
• Products | CO₂ + H₂O | CO and/or C (soot) + H₂O
• Flame | Blue, non-sooty | Yellow, sooty
• Heat released | Maximum | Less
• Hazard | Greenhouse gas CO₂ | Poisonous CO; soot
احتراق: آکسیجن کے ساتھ تعامل جس میں حرارت اور شعلہ نکلتا ہے۔ مکمل احتراق (زیادہ آکسیجن): CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + حرارت (نیلا شعلہ)۔ نامکمل احتراق (کم آکسیجن): CO اور کاربن (کالک) بنتے ہیں جو زہریلے اور نقصان دہ ہیں۔

══ KEY DIAGRAMS & FIGURES ══
1. Substitution of methane by chlorine: One H atom is replaced by one Cl atom in light.

- Hydrocarbons = C and H only. Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂: saturated, single covalent bonds; methane CH₄ (natural gas), ethane C₂H₆.
- Preparation:
  - Hydrogenation: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → C₂H₆; HC≡CH + 2H₂ → C₂H₆ (Ni, 200–300 °C, or Pt/Pd at room temp.).
  - Reduction of alkyl halides: Zn + HCl → nascent [H]; CH₃Cl + 2[H] → CH₄ + HCl.

الکینز سیر شدہ ہائیڈروکاربن ہیں (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂)۔ تیاری: ہائیڈروجنیشن (Ni، 200–300 °C)، الکائل ہیلائیڈ کی تخفیف (Zn/HCl) اور کریکنگ (450–750 °C)۔ یہ غیر متعامل ہیں مگر روشنی میں کلورین سے بدل کا تعامل اور آکسیجن میں احتراق کرتے ہیں۔

chapters.definitions:
• Hydrocarbon (ہائیڈروکاربن) [p. 196]: A compound containing carbon and hydrogen only.
• Alkane (الکین) [p. 196]: A saturated hydrocarbon with only single C–C bonds; general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
• Saturated hydrocarbon (سیر شدہ ہائیڈروکاربن) [p. 196]: A hydrocarbon in which all carbon–carbon bonds are single and each carbon holds the maximum number of H atoms.
• Hydrogenation (ہائیڈروجنیشن) [p. 196]: Addition of a hydrogen molecule across a carbon–carbon multiple bond in an unsaturated hydrocarbon.
• Nascent hydrogen (نومولود ہائیڈروجن) [p. 197]: Freshly produced atomic hydrogen [H], e.g. from Zn and HCl; a strong reducing agent.
• Reduction (of alkyl halide) (تخفیف) [p. 197]: Replacement of the halogen of an alkyl halide by hydrogen using nascent hydrogen to form an alkane.
• Cracking (کریکنگ) [p. 197]: Breaking large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes by heating (450–750 °C) at high pressure.
• Substitution reaction (بدل کا تعامل) [p. 198]: A reaction in which one atom or group of atoms is replaced by another atom or group of atoms.
• Photochemical reaction (ضیائی کیمیائی تعامل) [p. 197]: A chemical reaction that takes place in the presence of light.
• Halogenation (ہیلوجنیشن) [p. 197]: Reaction of an alkane with a halogen in light in which H atoms are substituted by halogen atoms.
• Combustion (احتراق) [p. 198]: Reaction of a substance with oxygen that rapidly releases heat and produces a flame.
• Incomplete combustion (نامکمل احتراق) [p. 198]: Burning in a limited supply of oxygen, producing CO and/or carbon and water.

══ BILINGUAL GLOSSARY ══
• Hydrocarbon (ہائیڈروکاربن): C and H only
• Alkane (الکین): Saturated hydrocarbon
• Hydrogenation (ہائیڈروجنیشن): Adding H₂
• Reduction (تخفیف): Adding hydrogen / removing halogen
• Nascent hydrogen (نومولود ہائیڈروجن): Atomic [H]
• Cracking (کریکنگ): Breaking big molecules
• Substitution (بدل): Replacement of an atom
• Photochemical (ضیائی کیمیائی): Needs light
• Combustion (احتراق): Burning in oxygen
• Soot (کالک): Carbon from incomplete burning
• Catalyst (عمل انگیز): Speeds up reaction
• Non-polar (غیر قطبی): No charge separation
chapters.formulasAndConcepts:
══ KEY FORMULAS & QUANTITIES ══
• Alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (Saturated)
• Hydrogenation catalyst: Ni, 200–300 °C (or Pt/Pd, room temp.)
• Reduction reagent: Zn + HCl(aq) → nascent [H]
• Cracking: 450–750 °C, high pressure (Gives alkanes + alkenes)
• Methane: CH₄ (Natural gas)
• Chloromethane: CH₃Cl (Mono-substitution product)

══ KEY EQUATIONS & DERIVATIONS ══
• CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ --Ni, 200–300 °C--> CH₃–CH₃ — Ethene → ethane.
• HC≡CH + 2H₂ --Ni, 200–300 °C--> CH₃–CH₃ — Ethyne → ethane.
• CH₃CH=CH₂ + H₂ --Ni--> CH₃CH₂CH₃ — Propene → propane.
• CH₃C≡CH + 2H₂ --Ni--> CH₃CH₂CH₃ — Propyne → propane.
• Zn + 2HCl -> ZnCl₂ + 2[H] — Nascent hydrogen.
• CH₃Cl + 2[H] --Zn/HCl--> CH₄ + HCl — Methyl chloride → methane.
• CH₃CH₂Cl + 2[H] --Zn/HCl--> CH₃CH₃ + HCl — Ethyl chloride → ethane.
• CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl + 2[H] --Zn/HCl--> CH₃CH₂CH₃ + HCl — Propyl chloride → propane.
• C₁₀H₂₂ --450–750 °C--> C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄ — Cracking of decane.
• CH₄ + Cl₂ --diffused sunlight--> CH₃Cl + HCl — Mono-substitution (photochemical).
• CH₄ + 2Cl₂ --direct sunlight--> C + 4HCl — Explosive.
• CH₄ + 2O₂ -> CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat — Complete combustion.
• 2CH₄ + 3O₂ -> 2CO + 4H₂O — Incomplete combustion (CO).
• CH₄ + O₂ -> C + 2H₂O — Incomplete combustion (soot).

══ CONCEPTUAL REASONING (SLO-BASED) ══
1. Why do we not get an alkane by adding chlorine to methane?
   Answer: Chlorine replaces H (substitution) to give a chloroalkane, not another alkane.
2. Why is a gas stove flame blue but a candle flame yellow?
   Answer: Methane burns completely (blue); the wax of a candle burns incompletely, glowing soot particles make the flame yellow.
3. Why must cracked products contain at least one alkene?
   Answer: There are not enough H atoms for all the smaller molecules to be alkanes: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ split into two pieces leaves one piece short of 2 H.

══ APPLIED & REAL-LIFE CONCEPTS ══
1. Why can using a gas heater in a closed room be dangerous?
   Answer: Limited oxygen causes incomplete combustion, producing poisonous, odourless carbon monoxide.
2. Why is hexane used to extract cooking oil from seeds?
   Answer: Hexane is non-polar and unreactive; oils dissolve in it, and it can be evaporated off afterwards.
chapters.solvedExamples:
══ WORKED TEXTBOOK EXAMPLES ══

1. Complete: (a) CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → ? (b) CH₃CH₂Br + 2[H] → ? (c) C₁₂H₂₆ → C₈H₁₈ + ?
   Solution: (a) CH₃CH₃ (ethane) (b) CH₃CH₃ + HBr (c) C₄H₈ (butene) – check: 12 − 8 = 4 C; 26 − 18 = 8 H.

2. Why does an alkyne add two molecules of hydrogen but an alkene only one?
   Solution: A triple bond contains two “extra” bonds beyond a single bond, so two H₂ molecules are needed to make it a single bond; a double bond needs only one H₂.
chapters.solvedExercises:
NBF Chapter 14 Exercises (199):

— Exercise MCQs —
i. Which molecule contains a carbon–carbon single bond? → A (Ethane) | Ethane CH₃–CH₃.
ii. Which product is obtained when chloromethane (methyl chloride) is reduced? → C (Methane) | CH₃Cl + 2[H] → CH₄ + HCl.
iii. By hydrogenation we mean the addition of: → A (Hydrogen) | Definition.
iv. Combustion of methane produces: → D (All of these) | CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat.
v. Reduction of chloromethane gives: → C (Methane) | Alkyl halide → alkane.

— Q2. Give short answers —
(i) Give three examples of saturated hydrocarbons.
   Answer: Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈ (also butane C₄H₁₀).
(ii) Draw the structure of ethane.
   Answer: H₃C–CH₃: two carbon atoms joined by a single bond; each carbon also bonded to three hydrogen atoms (six C–H bonds in total).
(iii) Draw structural formulae of an alkane containing five carbon atoms.
   Answer: Pentane C₅H₁₂: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃. (Branched isomers: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃ 2-methylbutane and C(CH₃)₄ 2,2-dimethylpropane.)
(iv) What do you mean by hydrogenation reaction? Give one example.
   Answer: Addition of hydrogen across a C=C or C≡C bond in the presence of Ni at 200–300 °C (or Pt/Pd). Example: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃CH₃.
(v) What is meant by cracking?
   Answer: Breaking of large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes by heating at 450–750 °C under high pressure, e.g. C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄.

— Q3–Q6. Descriptive questions —
3. Discuss methods for the preparation of ethane.
   Answer: 1. Hydrogenation of ethene: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ --Ni, 200–300 °C--> CH₃CH₃
2. Hydrogenation of ethyne: HC≡CH + 2H₂ --Ni, 200–300 °C--> CH₃CH₃
3. Reduction of ethyl chloride (Zn/HCl): CH₃CH₂Cl + 2[H] → CH₃CH₃ + HCl
4. Cracking of a larger alkane, e.g. C₄H₁₀ → C₂H₆ + C₂H₄ (gives a mixture).
4. Describe properties of alkanes.
   Answer: Physical: non-polar, insoluble in water, less dense than water; C₁–C₄ gases, C₅–C₁₇ liquids, higher ones solids; boiling point rises with chain length; colourless and odourless; good solvents (hexane extracts vegetable oil). Chemical: generally unreactive (strong non-polar single bonds, saturated); (i) combustion – complete: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat; incomplete: CO or C; (ii) substitution with chlorine in light – CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (diffused light); explosive in direct sunlight: CH₄ + 2Cl₂ → C + 4HCl.
5. Write a chemical equation to show the preparation of an alkane from an alkene and from an alkyne.
   Answer: Alkene: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ --Ni, 200–300 °C--> CH₃CH₃. Alkyne: HC≡CH + 2H₂ --Ni, 200–300 °C--> CH₃CH₃.
6. Write chemical equations for the preparation of propane.
   Answer: CH₃CH=CH₂ + H₂ --Ni--> CH₃CH₂CH₃ (from propene); CH₃C≡CH + 2H₂ --Ni--> CH₃CH₂CH₃ (from propyne); CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl + 2[H] --Zn/HCl--> CH₃CH₂CH₃ + HCl (from propyl chloride).
chapters.importantQuestions:
══ SHORT RESPONSE QUESTIONS (PAST PAPERS, MODEL PAPERS & SLO PRACTICE) ══

1. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] What are substitution reactions? Which type of compounds shows these reactions?
   Answer: Reactions in which one atom or group of atoms is replaced by another atom or group. They are shown by saturated compounds such as alkanes, e.g. CH₄ + Cl₂ --light--> CH₃Cl + HCl.

2. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] Why are alkanes called saturated hydrocarbons? Write their general formula to determine their molecular formula.
   Answer: Because all C–C bonds are single and each carbon is bonded to the maximum number of H atoms – no more H can be added. General formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂: for n = 3, C₃H₈ (propane).

3. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] Write chemical equations for the combustion of methane in (a) limited oxygen (b) excess oxygen.
   Answer: (a) 2CH₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO + 4H₂O (or CH₄ + O₂ → C + 2H₂O). (b) CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat.

4. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026 (Old-22)] Why are alkanes generally considered unreactive? Explain in the context of their structure.
   Answer: They contain only strong single covalent C–C and C–H bonds; C–H bonds are almost non-polar so there are no charged sites for reagents to attack; and being saturated they cannot undergo addition reactions.

5. [Verified Official - FBISE 2nd Annual 2025] What is a substitution reaction? Write the equation for halogenation of methane.
   Answer: Replacement of an atom/group by another atom/group. CH₄ + Cl₂ --diffused sunlight--> CH₃Cl + HCl.

6. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] Write reactions of alkanes for (a) complete combustion (b) incomplete combustion.
   Answer: (a) CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat (b) 2CH₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO + 4H₂O.

7. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] Write reactions of CH₄ with Cl₂ in (a) diffused sunlight/UV (b) direct sunlight.
   Answer: (a) CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (b) CH₄ + 2Cl₂ → C + 4HCl (explosive).

8. [Verified Official - FBISE 2nd Annual 2025] Write reactions for the preparation of alkanes: (a) ethane from ethyne (b) methane from methyl chloride.
   Answer: (a) HC≡CH + 2H₂ --Ni, 200–300 °C--> CH₃CH₃ (b) CH₃Cl + 2[H] --Zn/HCl--> CH₄ + HCl.

9. Define cracking and give one example with an equation.
   Answer: Breaking large alkanes into smaller alkanes and alkenes at 450–750 °C and high pressure: C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄.

10. Why are lighter alkanes used as fuels?
   Answer: Their combustion is controllable, they release a large amount of heat per gram, and they are cheap and readily available.


══ EXTENDED / LONG RESPONSE QUESTIONS ══

1. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] How can ethane be prepared by (a) hydrogenation of alkynes (b) reduction of alkyl halides? Give equations and conditions.
   Answer: (a) HC≡CH + 2H₂ --Ni, 200–300 °C (or Pt/Pd, room temp.)--> CH₃CH₃. (b) Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + 2[H]; CH₃CH₂Cl + 2[H] → CH₃CH₃ + HCl (nascent hydrogen from zinc and aqueous HCl reduces ethyl chloride).

2. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2026] What are substitution reactions? Why do alkanes show them? Illustrate the monosubstituted product of methane with Cl₂.
   Answer: Substitution: one atom/group replaced by another. Alkanes are saturated – they have no multiple bonds to add to – so they react by replacing H atoms. In light, light energy splits Cl₂ into Cl atoms which replace an H: CH₄ + Cl₂ --diffused sunlight--> CH₃Cl + HCl. Chloromethane displayed: C with three H and one Cl.

3. [Verified Official - FBISE 2nd Annual 2025] What are alkanes? Why are they unreactive? Give two methods of their preparation with equations.
   Answer: Saturated hydrocarbons CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ with only single bonds. Unreactive because of strong non-polar C–C and C–H bonds and no multiple bonds. Preparation: hydrogenation CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ --Ni--> CH₃CH₃; reduction CH₃Cl + 2[H] --Zn/HCl--> CH₄ + HCl (also cracking).

4. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] How can alkanes be prepared from alkynes and alkyl halides? Write balanced equations.
   Answer: From alkynes: HC≡CH + 2H₂ --Ni, 200–300 °C--> C₂H₆. From alkyl halides: CH₃CH₂Br + 2[H] --Zn/HCl--> C₂H₆ + HBr; CH₃Cl + 2[H] → CH₄ + HCl.

5. [Verified Official - FBISE Annual 2025] Describe the preparation of alkanes by hydrogenation of alkenes and by cracking of larger hydrocarbons.
   Answer: Hydrogenation: H₂ adds across C=C in the presence of Ni at 200–300 °C (or Pt/Pd): CH₃CH=CH₂ + H₂ → CH₃CH₂CH₃. Cracking: large alkanes heated at 450–750 °C and high pressure break into smaller alkanes and alkenes: C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄.

══ Chapter 14 in one page
- Hydrocarbons = C and H only. Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂: saturated, single covalent bonds; methane CH₄ (natural gas), ethane C₂H₆.
- Preparation:
  - Hydrogenation: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂ → C₂H₆; HC≡CH + 2H₂ → C₂H₆ (Ni, 200–300 °C, or Pt/Pd at room temp.).
  - Reduction of alkyl halides: Zn + HCl → nascent [H]; CH₃Cl + 2[H] → CH₄ + HCl.
  - Cracking: 450–750 °C, high pressure; C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄.
- Properties: non-polar, insoluble in water, less dense; C₁–C₄ gases, C₅–C₁₇ liquids; hexane as solvent. Unreactive (strong non-polar single bonds).
- Substitution (photochemical): CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (diffused light); CH₄ + 2Cl₂ → C + 4HCl (direct sunlight, explosive).
- Combustion: complete CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O + heat (blue flame); incomplete → CO or C (sooty). Fuels: controllable, high heat/gram, cheap.

chapters.title: Biochemistry
chapters.introduction:
Biochemistry is the chemistry of living things. Your brain and body work all day on the “fuel” that comes from food. This unit explains nutrition and a balanced diet, and the four main biomolecules – carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids – their sources, functions, how they are digested and what happens if they are lacking, plus the daily food intake for young adults and malnutrition.

Exam focus (3 summative SLOs): nutrition and healthy eating; the biomolecules with sources and functions (carbohydrates, proteins, lipids especially); carbohydrates as the main energy source. Asked as 3-mark short questions in almost every paper.

chapters.completeNotes:
══ FBISE ASSESSMENT & EXAM WEIGHTAGE ══
Exam focus (3 summative SLOs): nutrition and healthy eating; the biomolecules with sources and functions (carbohydrates, proteins, lipids especially); carbohydrates as the main energy source. Asked as 3-mark short questions in almost every paper.
Note: Energy values (4, 4 and 9 kcal per gram) and daily-intake figures are as given in the textbook (Figure 15.8). Two review MCQs have weak keys and are flagged.

══ 15.1 Nutrition, healthy eating and a balanced diet (pp. 201–202) ══
Nutrition is the process of taking in and using food (nutrients) that living things need to stay alive, grow, get energy and repair their bodies. The total of nutrients we take is our diet.
Why living organisms need food: (1) energy for all activities, including the brain working 24/7; (2) growth and making new cells; (3) repair of damaged tissues; (4) to regulate body processes and fight disease.
Importance of a healthy diet:
- Reduces high blood pressure and lowers high cholesterol.
- Helps prevent obesity, diabetes, heart (cardiovascular) disease, some cancers and bone problems.
- Improves bone health, muscle strength, brain function and immunity.
Balanced diet: a diet that provides all the nutrients in suitable amounts and proportions – carbohydrates, proteins, lipids (fats), vitamins, minerals, water and dietary fibre – to meet the body's needs for energy and health.
Biochemistry combines biology and chemistry: the study of organic and inorganic molecules in living organisms.
غذائیت وہ عمل ہے جس میں جاندار زندہ رہنے، توانائی، نشوونما اور مرمت کے لیے غذا لیتے اور استعمال کرتے ہیں۔ متوازن غذا میں کاربوہائیڈریٹس، پروٹین، چکنائی، وٹامن، معدنیات، پانی اور ریشہ مناسب مقدار میں ہوتے ہیں۔ صحت مند غذا بلڈ پریشر، کولیسٹرول، موٹاپے، شوگر اور دل کی بیماریوں سے بچاتی ہے۔

══ 15.2 Carbohydrates – the main energy source (pp. 202–203, 206) ══
Carbohydrates (“hydrates of carbon”) are biomolecules made of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, often with formula Cₓ(H₂O)y. Their primary function is to supply energy to all body cells.
1 g of carbohydrate → 4 kcal of energy.
In digestion carbohydrates are broken down to glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆), which cells oxidise in respiration:
C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + energy
Glucose is the preferred fuel of the brain. If the body lacks carbohydrates, it breaks down muscle protein and body fat for energy. Extra glucose is stored as glycogen (liver and muscles) or converted to fat.
Classification:
- Monosaccharides (one sugar unit): glucose, fructose.
- Disaccharides (two units): sucrose (table sugar), lactose (milk sugar), maltose.
- Polysaccharides (many units): starch (plants), glycogen (animals), cellulose (fibre).
Sources: cereals and grains (wheat, rice, maize, oats), potatoes, bread, fruits, sugar, honey, milk and yogurt, beans and pulses.
Other roles: fibre helps digestion and makes you feel full; can be converted into fats and amino acids.
Deficiency: headache, fatigue, weakness, difficulty concentrating, nausea, constipation, bad breath, muscle loss.
[Table: Types of carbohydrates]
Type | Sugar units | Examples
• Monosaccharide | One | Glucose, fructose
• Disaccharide | Two | Sucrose, lactose, maltose
• Polysaccharide | Three or more (many) | Starch, glycogen, cellulose
Exam Tip: “Carbohydrates are the major source of energy – defend.” They are quickly digested to glucose, soluble and easily oxidised in respiration, the brain depends on glucose, and they form the largest part of our diet.
کاربوہائیڈریٹس کاربن، ہائیڈروجن اور آکسیجن سے بنے ہیں اور جسم کی بنیادی توانائی کا ذریعہ ہیں (1 گرام = 4 کلو کیلوری)۔ یہ گلوکوز میں ٹوٹتے ہیں جو دماغ کا پسندیدہ ایندھن ہے۔ اقسام: مونو سیکرائیڈ (گلوکوز)، ڈائی سیکرائیڈ (سکروز، لیکٹوز)، پولی سیکرائیڈ (نشاستہ، گلائیکوجن)۔ ذرائع: گندم، چاول، آلو، پھل، دودھ، دالیں۔

══ 15.3 Proteins and amino acids (pp. 203–204, 207) ══
Proteins are large biomolecules (macromolecules) made of long chains of amino acids joined by peptide bonds. They contain C, H, O, N (and often S). Every cell contains protein.
1 g of protein → 4 kcal of energy.
Functions of proteins:
1. Growth, building and repair of body tissues and cells (muscle, skin, hair, nails); essential for wound healing.
2. Enzymes – proteins that act as biological catalysts and speed up chemical reactions (e.g. digestion: amylase, pepsin).
3. Hormones (chemical messengers), e.g. insulin.
4. Antibodies – defence against infection (immune system).
5. Transport, e.g. haemoglobin carries oxygen in the blood.
6. Structure: collagen, keratin; energy source when carbohydrates are short.
Digestion: proteins are digested in the stomach and small intestine and absorbed as amino acids, which the body uses to make its own proteins.
Sources: animal – meat, fish, eggs, milk, cheese; plant – beans, pulses (lentils), soya beans, nuts, peas.
Deficiency: stunted growth in children, brittle hair and nails, poor wound healing, muscle loss and weakness/fatigue, weight loss, anaemia, weak immunity, kwashiorkor (swelling).
پروٹین امینو ایسڈز کی لمبی زنجیریں ہیں جو پیپٹائڈ بانڈ سے جڑی ہوتی ہیں (1 گرام = 4 کلو کیلوری)۔ افعال: جسم کی نشوونما اور مرمت، انزائمز (حیاتیاتی عمل انگیز)، ہارمونز، اینٹی باڈیز اور ہیموگلوبن کے ذریعے آکسیجن کی ترسیل۔ ذرائع: گوشت، مچھلی، انڈے، دودھ، دالیں، سویا بین۔ کمی سے بچوں کی نشوونما رکتی ہے اور پٹھے کمزور ہوتے ہیں۔

══ 15.4 Lipids (fats and oils) (pp. 204–205, 207) ══
Lipids are fatty, waxy or oily organic compounds – fatty acids or their derivatives – that are insoluble in water (polar solvent) but soluble in organic solvents such as alcohol and chloroform. They include fats, oils, waxes and steroids (cholesterol).
Lipids are mostly hydrocarbon chains with little oxygen, so they are an excellent energy store: 1 g of lipid → 9 kcal (more than twice carbohydrates).
Functions:
1. Energy reserve (long-term storage in fat tissue).
2. Part of cell membranes – control what enters and leaves cells.
3. Absorption of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K.
4. Making hormones (steroid hormones).
5. Insulation to keep the body warm and protection/cushioning of organs.
Digestion: digested in the small intestine and absorbed as fatty acids and glycerol.
Sources: animal – butter, ghee, milk, cheese, meat, eggs (rich in saturated fats and cholesterol); plant – sunflower, olive, corn, canola oil, nuts, avocado (rich in unsaturated fats, healthier).
Deficiency: dry skin/rashes, hair loss, weaker immunity, poor growth in children, vitamin A/D/E/K deficiency.
Excess: obesity, high cholesterol, heart disease. Most cholesterol is made by the liver.
لپڈز (چکنائیاں اور تیل) پانی میں حل نہیں ہوتے مگر کلوروفارم جیسے نامیاتی محللات میں حل ہوتے ہیں۔ 1 گرام = 9 کلو کیلوری۔ افعال: توانائی کا ذخیرہ، خلیے کی جھلی کا حصہ، وٹامن A، D، E، K کا جذب، ہارمون بنانا اور جسم کو گرم رکھنا۔ ذرائع: گھی، مکھن، پنیر، گوشت (سیر شدہ)، سورج مکھی اور زیتون کا تیل، میوے (غیر سیر شدہ)۔

══ 15.5 Nucleic acids: DNA and RNA (pp. 205, 208) ══
Nucleic acids are large biomolecules that carry genetic information and control protein synthesis. Their building blocks are nucleotides (each = sugar + phosphate + nitrogenous base).
- DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid): double-stranded (double helix); sugar deoxyribose; stores all the genetic information of a person and passes it from one generation to the next; found mainly in the nucleus.
- RNA (ribonucleic acid): single-stranded; sugar ribose; copies (expresses) the genetic code from DNA and uses it to make proteins (converts gene information into amino-acid sequences).
Sources: all cells contain nucleic acids; seeds, grains, fish eggs, meat and fish are good sources (the body makes its own).
Disorders linked to faulty nucleic-acid metabolism: Lesch–Nyhan syndrome (rare congenital disorder affecting the brain and behaviour); ataxia-telangiectasia (Louis–Bar syndrome) affecting movement and speech.
[Table: DNA vs RNA]
DNA | RNA
• Double-stranded (double helix) | Single-stranded
• Sugar: deoxyribose | Sugar: ribose
• Bases A, T, G, C | Bases A, U, G, C
• Stores genetic information | Uses genetic information to make proteins
• Mainly in the nucleus | Nucleus and cytoplasm
نیوکلیک ایسڈز جینیاتی معلومات رکھتے اور پروٹین سازی کو کنٹرول کرتے ہیں؛ ان کی اکائی نیوکلیوٹائڈ ہے۔ DNA دوہری لڑی والا ہے اور جینیاتی معلومات محفوظ رکھ کر اگلی نسل تک پہنچاتا ہے؛ RNA اکہری لڑی والا ہے اور یہ معلومات پروٹین بنانے میں استعمال کرتا ہے۔

══ 15.6 Daily intake for young adults and malnutrition (pp. 208–210) ══
A healthy diet needs macronutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats), micronutrients (vitamins and minerals) and enough water, from a variety of foods in each food group. Tips: eat less sugar, salt and fat, more fruits, vegetables and whole grains.
Daily food intake for young adults (textbook Figure 15.8, two age/sex groups):
- Grains: about 3–8 bowls
- Vegetables: at least 3 servings
- Fruits: at least 2 servings
- Meat, fish, egg and alternatives: about 200–400 g
- Milk and alternatives: 1–2 servings
- Fat/oil, salt and sugar: eat the least
- Fluids: 6–8 glasses of water
Fat should be the smallest part of the diet (roughly 20–35% of energy, mostly unsaturated) because it is energy-dense (9 kcal/g) and excess causes obesity and heart disease.
Calorie: energy needed to raise 1 g of water by 1 °C; food energy is measured in kilocalories. High-calorie-density foods (fried, sugary, fast food) raise the risk of weight gain, obesity and high blood pressure; low-calorie-density foods (vegetables, fruit) give more water and fibre and fill you up.
Malnutrition: a condition when the body does not get the right amount of nutrients – either undernourished or over-nourished.
Marasmus: severe undernutrition – deficiency of all macronutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats) – causing extreme thinness and wasting.
نوجوانوں کی روزانہ غذا: اناج 3–8 پیالے، سبزیاں کم از کم 3، پھل کم از کم 2، گوشت/مچھلی/انڈے 200–400 گرام، دودھ 1–2، پانی 6–8 گلاس؛ چکنائی، نمک اور چینی سب سے کم۔ غذائی قلت کم یا زیادہ غذائیت دونوں سے ہوتی ہے۔ میراسمس تمام بڑے غذائی اجزا کی شدید کمی سے ہونے والی بیماری ہے۔

══ CHAPTER SUMMARY TABLES ══

Biomolecule | Sources | Main functions | Deficiency effects
• Carbohydrates | Grains, rice, potatoes, fruits, milk, beans | Main energy source (4 kcal/g); fibre aids digestion | Fatigue, headache, weakness, poor concentration, constipation

• Nucleic acids | All cells; seeds, grains, fish eggs, meat | Store and transmit genetic information; protein synthesis | Rare genetic disorders (Lesch–Nyhan, ataxia-telangiectasia)

══ KEY DIAGRAMS & FIGURES ══
1. Energy per gram of nutrient: Lipids give more than twice the energy of carbohydrates or proteins.
